title: 6.4 Ecological Succession
description: Primary and secondary succession, pioneer species, climax community, and changes in ecosystems over time

questions.question: What is the gradual and predictable change in the species composition of an ecosystem over time called?
Which type of succession begins in an area where no soil exists, such as on bare rock?
Which type of succession occurs in an area where a disturbance has removed an existing community but left soil intact?
What are the first organisms to colonize a bare rock or lifeless area during primary succession called?
Which of the following is an example of a pioneer species on bare rock?
How do pioneer species like lichens contribute to soil formation?
options: They produce large amounts of leaves
They secrete acids that break down rock into soil particles
They bring soil from other areas
They absorb nutrients from the air only

questions.question: Which group of organisms typically follows lichens and mosses in primary succession?
What is the correct sequence of seres in primary succession on bare rock?
options: Lichens and mosses → grasses → shrubs → trees

questions.question: Which type of succession is faster: primary or secondary?
Why is secondary succession faster than primary succession?
options: Because it starts on bare rock
Because pioneer species are not needed
Because animals bring seeds from other areas

questions.question: Which of the following events can trigger secondary succession?
Which of the following is an example of primary succession?
options: Growth of plants on a newly formed volcanic island
Regrowth after an abandoned farm field

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secondary succession?
options: Colonization of bare rock by lichens
Regrowth of a forest after deforestation
Mosses growing on a newly exposed rock surface

questions.question: A stable, self-sustaining community at the end of ecological succession is called the:
Which of the following is a characteristic of a climax community?
options: It is stable and changes very little over time
It consists only of pioneer species
It is the first stage of succession

questions.question: In a tropical region, what type of climax community is most likely to develop?
What role do mosses play in primary succession?
options: They are the final climax species
They help trap moisture and build soil
They prevent other plants from growing
They fix nitrogen from the atmosphere

questions.question: After a wildfire destroys a forest, the process of regrowth is an example of:
Which term describes each intermediate stage of succession?
What happens to biodiversity during the process of ecological succession?
options: It generally increases until the climax community

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a human activity that can initiate secondary succession?
In primary succession on a newly formed volcanic island, which group of organisms would appear first?
What happens to soil depth and quality as succession progresses from pioneer to climax community?
Which of the following best describes the difference between primary and secondary succession?
options: Primary occurs in forests; secondary occurs in deserts
Primary starts without soil; secondary starts with soil
Secondary occurs only in aquatic ecosystems
